title: Modern Reversible Contraceptive Options in Ethiopia
sourceOrganization: Ethiopian Federal Ministry of Health (FMoH) & Marie Stopes Ethiopia
summary: Overview of free, safe, reversible contraceptive methods available across Ethiopian public health posts, health centers, and NGO clinics.
keyPoints: Implants (Implanon NXT / Jadelle): Small flexible rod under the arm; >99% effective for 3 to 5 years; immediate fertility return on removal.
3-Month Injectable (Depo-Provera): Discreet injection every 12-13 weeks; safe during breastfeeding; does not require daily memory.
Copper IUD: Non-hormonal T-device placed in the uterus; lasts up to 10-12 years with natural monthly periods.
Oral Contraceptive Pills: Combined or progestin-only pills taken once daily at the same time.
detailedContent: Family planning is completely free of charge in public Ethiopian health facilities under the national reproductive health strategy.
Youth aged 15-24 have the legal and clinical right to access confidential Youth-Friendly Services (YFS) without parental or partner consent.
whenToSeeClinician: Visit your local Kebele Health Post or Woreda Health Center to consult a midwife or HEW on the method best suited for your lifestyle.
ethiopiaContext: Free of charge at all public Kebele Health Posts and Woreda Health Centers; Marie Stopes toll-free 8044.

title: Emergency Contraception (Postinor-2 & Copper IUD)
sourceOrganization: World Health Organization (WHO) & Ethiopian Ministry of Health
summary: Emergency methods to prevent unintended pregnancy after unprotected intercourse, condom breakage, or missed contraceptive pills.
keyPoints: Emergency Contraceptive Pills (Postinor-2 / Levonorgestrel 1.5mg): Most effective when taken within 24 hours, but works up to 72 to 120 hours.
Available over-the-counter at licensed pharmacies and free/subsidized at Health Centers and Marie Stopes clinics in Ethiopia.
Does NOT induce abortion: Works by delaying ovulation and cannot terminate an established pregnancy.
Copper IUD insertion within 5 days (120 hours) of unprotected intercourse is >99% effective and provides ongoing protection for 10 years.
detailedContent: Emergency contraception is designed as a safety backup, not regular ongoing contraception.
Emergency pills do not protect against HIV or other sexually transmitted infections; if potential HIV exposure occurred, seek PEP within 72 hours.
whenToSeeClinician: Consult a pharmacist or health center as soon as possible after unprotected intercourse. The sooner taken, the higher the efficacy.
ethiopiaContext: Available over-the-counter at community pharmacies across Ethiopia; also provided at Marie Stopes clinics (Helpline: 8044).

title: የድንገተኛ የወሊድ መከላከያ (ፖስቲኖር-2 እና የኮፐር ሉፕ)
sourceOrganization: የዓለም ጤና ድርጅት (WHO) እና የኢትዮጵያ ጤና ጥበቃ ሚኒስቴር (FMoH)
summary: ያለ መከላከያ የግብረ-ስጋ ግንኙነት ከተፈጸመ በኋላ ያልተፈለገ እርግዝናን ለመከላከል የሚያገለግሉ የድንገተኛ ዘዴዎች (ፖስቲኖር-2 ወይም የኮፐር ሉፕ)።
keyPoints: የድንገተኛ የወሊድ መከላከያ እንክብል (ፖስቲኖር-2 / Levonorgestrel 1.5mg)፡ ግንኙነት ከተፈጸመ በኋላ በተቻለ ፍጥነት መወሰድ አለበት (በተለይ በ24 ሰዓታት ውስጥ፣ ነገር ግን እስከ 72-120 ሰዓታት/3-5 ቀናት ይሰራል)።
ፅንስ አያስወርድም፡ የእንቁላል መፈጠርን (ovulation) በማዘግየት እርግዝና እንዳይፈጠር ይከላከላል እንጂ የተፈጠረን እርግዝና አያቋርጥም።
ከኤችአይቪ ወይም ከአባላዘር በሽታዎች አይከላከልም፡ የኤችአይቪ ተጋላጭነት ካለ በ72 ሰዓታት ውስጥ የድንገተኛ መከላከያ መድኃኒት (PEP) መጀመር አለብዎት።
የኮፐር ማህፀን ሉፕ (Copper IUD)፡ ግንኙነት ከተፈጸመ በ5 ቀናት (120 ሰዓታት) ውስጥ በጤና ባለሙያ ቢገባ ከ99% በላይ ውጤታማ ሲሆን ለ10 ዓመታት ቀጣይነት ያለው ጥበቃ ይሰጣል።
detailedContent: የድንገተኛ የወሊድ መከላከያ ለአደጋ ጊዜ ብቻ የሚያገለግል እንጂ መደበኛ የወሊድ መከላከያ አይደለም።
በኢትዮጵያ ውስጥ በማንኛውም የማህበረሰብ ፋርማሲ ያለ ሀኪም ማዘዣ በግል መግዛት ይቻላል፤ በማሪ ስቶፕስ ክሊኒኮች እና በጤና ጣቢያዎችም ይገኛል።
whenToSeeClinician: ግንኙነት ከተፈጸመ በኋላ በተቻለ ፍጥነት በአቅራቢያዎ የሚገኝ ፋርማሲ፣ ጤና ጣቢያ ወይም የማሪ ስቶፕስ ክሊኒክ (በነጻ የስልክ መስመር 8044) ያማክሩ።
ethiopiaContext: በሁሉም የማህበረሰብ ፋርማሲዎች ያለ ማዘዣ ይገኛል፤ በማሪ ስቶፕስ ክሊኒኮች (ነጻ መስመር፡ 8044) እና በመንግስት ጤና ጣቢያዎች ይሰጣል።

title: Dual Protection: Condoms with Long-Acting Contraception
summary: Using condoms simultaneously with an implant, IUD, or injectable achieves dual protection against both pregnancy and STIs/HIV.
keyPoints: Implants, IUDs, and injectables protect exceptionally well against pregnancy but offer ZERO defense against HIV or STIs.
Male and female latex condoms are the only barrier method that physically blocks transmission of HIV, syphilis, and gonorrhea.
Dual protection ensures both partners maintain optimal reproductive health without compromise.
Condoms are distributed free of charge at all public health facilities and youth centers in Ethiopia.
detailedContent: In Ethiopia, public health campaigns encourage adolescents and young adults to adopt dual protection consistently.
Correct and consistent condom use involves checking expiry dates, opening packaging carefully, leaving a reservoir tip, and single-use disposal.
whenToSeeClinician: Collect free condoms at your Kebele Health Post or youth corner and discuss long-acting reversible options with your clinician.
ethiopiaContext: Promoted across Ethiopian universities, vocational colleges, and community youth centers.

title: DMPA-SC (Sayana Press) Subcutaneous Self-Injection Pilot
sourceOrganization: PATH & Ethiopian Federal Ministry of Health (FMoH)
summary: Draft protocol for home self-injection of 3-month subcutaneous medroxyprogesterone acetate (Sayana Press) using a prefilled all-in-one device.
keyPoints: Sayana Press is a prefilled single-use injection device with a small needle administered under the skin of the abdomen or thigh.
Provides 3 months of contraceptive protection with lower hormone dose than intramuscular Depo-Provera.
Trained women can self-administer at home without clinic visits after receiving HEW demonstration.
Safe storage and sharps container disposal are essential home requirements.
detailedContent: Draft clinical notes: Pilot implementation study guidelines across select agrarian woredas in Oromia, Amhara, and Sidama regions.
Pending final national regulatory rollout by the Ethiopian Food and Drug Authority (EFDA).
whenToSeeClinician: Ask your Health Extension Worker whether the Sayana Press demonstration pilot is operational in your woreda.
ethiopiaContext: Currently undergoing regional pilot evaluation in selected woredas in Ethiopia.
